results.correct_value: 5.12 range: header 5.12- stays; Crowds should not say 5.12+
results.evidence: The route page lists the route at 5.12- with a 5.11 V5 crux on P4. The first-ascent account in the journal of record calls it 5.12+ overall but describes mostly 5.10-5.11 climbing with a few short bouldery bits in the 5.12 range; the first ascensionist's own write-up says the whole thing goes at 5.11-something with the crux perhaps 5.12b. No two sources agree on a sub-grade, but all agree it is a 5.12 route, so the Crowds '5.12+' (the only field contradicting the 5.12- header) is reduced to '5.12'; the 5.12- header and the 5.12b pitch note (a 5.12- route with a 5.12a/b crux) are compatible. Note: the FA write-up says the crux may be more like 5.12b for TALLER climbers, while the row's overview/hazards say shorter climbers find it harder — left untouched (one source only).

results.correct_value: P1-3 and P5 need only draws plus a couple of cams; P4 (2 bolts at the crux) and P6-8 need a standard cam rack
results.evidence: The first ascensionist's write-up states the first 3 pitches and pitch 5 are adequately protected with just quickdraws and maybe a finger piece or two, while P4, 6, 7 and 8 require a standard cam rack, and that the crux sequence has 2 bolts. The route page's P4 description advises long slings and/or backcleaning or running it out low on the pitch, i.e. gear placements. So gear[1] is correct and pro_needs ('mostly bolt-protected on the lower 5 pitches') is the outlier; the pitch_detail note (bolts back up the crux) is also correct.

patches.find: Mostly bolt-protected on the lower 5 pitches with a couple of cams recommended; gear-protected thin crack and splitter pitches higher up.
patches.replace: Pitches 1-3 and 5 are mostly bolt-protected and need only a couple of cams; pitch 4 has two bolts at its crux but needs a cam rack for the rest, as do the thin crack and splitter pitches higher up.

results.fact: Blue Lake Trailhead distance from Washington Pass
results.evidence: bivy-only dispute: the shared 'Blue Lake trailhead roadside bivy' card's 'half a mile west of Washington Pass' is regional camp-list text; bivy[] is owned by the camping clean-up, so no patch. The entry does serve this route's trailhead area.

The Trailhead waypoint says 5,200 ft while the trailhead card says 5,400 ft. The USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation service returns 5,380 ft at the stored trailhead coordinate (48.5191, -120.6742), and an independent Blue Lake trail guide gives the trailhead's starting elevation as 5,380 ft. The 5,400 ft in trailheadDirection is a fair rounding; the waypoint's 5,200 is the outlier.

results.fact: Blue Lake Trailhead distance from Washington Pass
results.evidence: Sources disagree: one club route page says 1.5 mi west of Washington Pass; the state trail association says a little under a mile past the Washington Pass Overlook; the Forest Service page says about 0.25 mi beyond the Overlook; another guide puts the trailhead at milepost 161 while the pass is 0.3 mi past milepost 162 (~1.3 mi). Straight-line from the pass (48.5236,-120.6547) to the trailhead coordinate is ~0.95 mi, so 0.5 mi is too short, but 1 vs 1.5 mi cannot be settled by two agreeing sources. Would be settled by a measured road distance from the pass summit to the lot. The bivy card's half-mile belongs to the bivy clean-up.

Two sources give the traverse as 26 pitches (the route page: 2,000 ft, 26 pitches, Grade V; a first-hand trip report: 26 pitches over two Grade III and three Grade II routes). The breakdown's per-section counts (4+3+?+5+7) are each constituent route's own pitch count and sum to about 22-23; the gap is presumably connecting/scrambling pitches, but no source itemises the 26, so neither figure can be changed. Would be settled by a source listing how the 26 are counted.

results.correct_value: About a dozen or more across the day (2 Liberty Bell, 2 Concord, 1-2 Lexington, 5-6 NEWS west face, 2-3 SEWS)
results.evidence: The row's own breakdown and descent text describe rappels off every summit (back into the Liberty-Concord notch, two off Concord, a rappel plus a short one off Lexington, several down NEWS's west face, 2-3 off SEWS), so '5-6' — which is only the NEWS count — is the outlier. The traverse route page agrees: two steep rappels from Concord, a sequence of 5-6 rappels down NEWS's west face, and 3 rappels to the ground off SEWS; the NEWS Northwest Corner page likewise gives 6 rappels down the west face. Written as per-summit prose, not a bare number.

patches.value: About a dozen or more across the day, spread over every summit: two back into the Liberty Bell-Concord notch, two short ones off Concord Tower, one or two off Lexington Tower, five or six down North Early Winters Spire's west face, and two or three off South Early Winters Spire.

results.correct_value: Doubles about 2-4 in plus a single #5 (NEWS wide pitch; also SEWS Bear Hug)
results.evidence: For North Early Winters Spire's NW Corner, its route page calls for a standard rack to 4 or 5 inches for the offwidth pitch, and a detailed trip report recommends doubles of 2-4 with a single #5. For South Early Winters Spire's SW Rib, multiple reports name a #4 and #5 for the Bear Hug offwidth. So the gear list is right and the rack/Protection summaries ('a couple bigger pieces to 3-4in') understate it.
